# The Agent Engineer — Full Curriculum Detail (for AI agents)

> Extended machine-readable outline of both learning tracks at https://balajichippada.com/ — the
> paid flagship course "Agentic AI at Production Level" (16 modules, 265 lessons) and the
> free 26-week Agentic AI Engineer Roadmap (9 phases). Summary: https://balajichippada.com/llms.txt

## Site purpose

Learning platform by Balaji Chippada for engineers who want to build production agentic AI — RAG,
tools, MCP, LangGraph, multi-agent systems, evaluation, guardrails, deployment and monitoring.
Two tracks: a structured paid course that starts from zero Python, and a free open roadmap.
Live masterclasses run alongside both.

---

# Part 1 — Course: "Agentic AI at Production Level"

## Course facts

- **Format**: Self-paced
- **Access**: 2 years + all updates
- **Level**: Starter → advanced
- **Prereqs**: Start from scratch — no experience needed
- **Projects**: Hands-on production builds
- **Certificate**: Verified on completion
- **Scale**: 16 modules, 265 lessons
- **Price**: ₹29,999 (Launch offer — First 45 days, through 2026-10-09); regular price ₹34,999
- **Tax**: 18% GST is already included and paid to the Government.
- **Payment**: One-time. No subscription.

## What is included

- Weekly live sessions on the latest topics
- Session recordings available for 2 years
- Private WhatsApp community
- Production-ready starter templates & code reviews
- Quiz after every video; multiple assignments per module with concrete inputs, a deliverable, and "done when" criteria
- Doubts answered within 24 working hours
- 2 one-to-one mock interviews with feedback, plus resume preparation
- Biweekly content updates; 2 years of access covering every update in that window
- Certificate awarded only after the full course, all assignments reviewed and approved, and all mock interviews

## The through-line project: "Atlas"

One product is carried through the entire course and upgraded module by module — from a plain LLM
client to a ReAct agent, then grounded with RAG, connected over MCP, given memory, re-architected on
LangGraph, evaluated, split into a multi-agent team, locked down with guardrails, deployed, and
finally monitored in production.

## Modules (16)

### Module 01 — Python Fundamentals (32 lessons · 8h 59m)

The Python you actually need before touching an LLM — from Colab setup to file handling.

- **You will build**: Command your Python basics: data structures, control flow, functions & file I/O
- **Tools**: Python, Google Colab

### Module 02 — Advanced Python (22 lessons · 5h 31m)

The Python that agent frameworks are actually written in — OOP, APIs, and your first LangChain build.

- **You will build**: Your own mini LangChain, built from scratch and installable as a package
- **Tools**: Python OOP, Dataclasses, requests, OpenAI & Groq APIs, LangChain

### Module 03 — NLP Basics, Intuition-First (17 lessons · 5h 26m)

Understand what text becomes before an LLM ever sees it.

- **You will build**: Semantic search over your own notes
- **Tools**: Tokens, Embeddings, Vector similarity, Transformers

### Module 04 — LLM Internals and LangChain (17 lessons · 5h 53m)

Pick and control the right model for a job — and predict its cost.

- **You will build**: A cost-aware LLM client: multi-turn chat, controlled output, the right model per job
- **Tools**: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, LangChain

### Module 05 — Prompt Engineering (24 lessons · 9h 05m)

Reliably get the behavior you want — the skill every agent call depends on.

- **You will build**: A pattern library of prompts you'll reuse in every agent call
- **Tools**: Prompt patterns, Structured output

### Module 06 — Foundations of Agentic Systems (18 lessons)

Understand the agent loop deeply — because you built it by hand.

- **You will build**: Atlas gets a ReAct brain, live tools, and self-correction
- **Tools**: ReAct, Tool calling, Plan-and-Solve

### Module 07 — RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation (24 lessons)

Answer from your own documents — grounded and cited, not from memory.

- **You will build**: Document intelligence for Atlas — grounded, cited answers
- **Tools**: Vector DBs, Chunking, Reranking, Graph RAG

### Module 08 — MCP — Model Context Protocol (17 lessons)

Connect your agent to anything through one universal standard.

- **You will build**: An MCP server from scratch + a Gmail & Calendar MCP for Atlas
- **Tools**: MCP, Gmail API, Calendar API

### Module 09 — Memory & Optimization (13 lessons)

Remember across sessions without blowing the context window.

- **You will build**: Atlas remembers your preferences across sessions — on a token budget
- **Tools**: Vector memory, Context engineering, Token budgeting

### Module 10 — State Machines & DAGs (LangGraph) (13 lessons)

Control an agent's flow deterministically — and pause for a human.

- **You will build**: Atlas re-architected on LangGraph with approval checkpoints
- **Tools**: LangGraph, State machines, Human-in-the-loop

### Module 11 — Evaluation (10 lessons)

Prove your agent works and catch regressions before users do.

- **You will build**: A regression suite that blocks bad Atlas changes
- **Tools**: LLM-as-Judge, Eval datasets, Trajectory benchmarks

### Module 12 — Multi-Agent Orchestration (11 lessons)

Make specialized agents collaborate without burning $400 in a loop.

- **You will build**: Atlas becomes a researcher + writer + critic team
- **Tools**: LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI

### Module 13 — Security & Guardrails (12 lessons)

Survive malicious users and handle sensitive data safely.

- **You will build**: Atlas locked down — guardrails, least privilege, PII redaction
- **Tools**: Guardrails, Prompt-injection defense, Sandboxing

### Module 14 — Deployment (incl. FastAPI) (12 lessons)

Real users can use your agent over the internet.

- **You will build**: Atlas live on the internet with a chat UI
- **Tools**: FastAPI, Docker, Async, CI/CD

### Module 15 — Monitoring & Operations (11 lessons)

See what your live agent is doing, what it costs, and how to improve it.

- **You will build**: A cost & quality dashboard for live Atlas
- **Tools**: Langfuse, LangSmith, Tracing

### Module 16 — Capstone Projects & Portfolio (12 lessons)

Ship and monitor your OWN agentic product — portfolio-ready.

- **You will build**: Your own agentic product — built, deployed, monitored
- **Tools**: Full production stack, Portfolio, Interview prep

## Hands-on projects (9)

- **Mini LangChain From Scratch** — Build the core building blocks behind LangChain — model loading, chat-model abstractions, provider integrations, and APIs.
  Tags: Python OOPs, Abstractions, Model Providers, Streaming, APIs
- **Semantic Search Over Your Documents** — Use embedding models and cosine similarity to build a semantic search engine over your own documents — from chunking to top-K results.
  Tags: Embeddings, Semantic Search, Cosine Similarity, Vector Store, Python
- **Multi-Model Chatbot With Full Control** — Build a powerful chatbot that lets users switch providers and tune temperature, reasoning, and streaming with LangChain and Streamlit.
  Tags: LangChain, Multi-Model, Custom Parameters, Streaming, Streamlit, Python
- **Upgrade Your Chatbot With Advanced Prompting** — Add prompt templates, versioning, LCEL chains, conversation history, and prompt caching for faster, more reliable responses.
  Tags: Prompt Templates, Prompt Versioning, LCEL, Conversation History, Prompt Caching, Python
- **Upgrade Your Chatbot With Agentic Power** — Add an agentic loop with Plan-Act-Observe-Reflect, powerful tools, self-correction, retry limits, and a plan-and-solve strategy.
  Tags: Agentic Loop, Tools, Web Search, Email Reader, APIs, Self-Correction, Retry & Limits, Plan & Solve, Python
- **Advanced RAG System** — Build a production-ready RAG system with advanced indexing, hybrid search, reranking, low-latency design, evaluations, and RBAC.
  Tags: Indexing Pipeline, Hybrid Search, Reranking, Metadata Filtering, Low Latency, Evaluations, RBAC, Production Ready, Python
- **Build MCP Server for Google Services & Integrate with Chatbot** — Build an MCP server from scratch for Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, and more, then integrate it with a LangChain chatbot.
  Tags: MCP, MCP from Scratch, Google Calendar, Gmail, Google Drive, OAuth 2.0, LangChain Agent, Secure & Scalable, Python
- **Memory-Powered Personalized Chatbot** — Add short-term, summary, long-term, profile, and episodic memory with intelligent recall for smarter, personalized conversations.
  Tags: Conversation Buffer, Summarization, Vector DB, User Profiles, Episodic Memory, Memory Router, Personalization, Python
- **LangGraph Multi-Agent System** — Build planner, researcher, coder, and reviewer agents that collaborate through A2A and M2M protocols with shared tools and memory.
  Tags: LangGraph, Multi-Agent, A2A Protocol, M2M Protocol, Shared Memory, Scalable, Production Ready

The course also includes 3 capstone projects and 2 personal projects.

## Who the course is for

- Complete beginners — no Python, no AI/ML background, no CS degree, no work experience required
- Working software engineers targeting roles like Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) who can code but
  have never taken an agent to production: evaluation, observability, guardrails, memory, cost
  control and deployment are where the course spends its time

# Part 2 — Free 26-week Agentic AI Engineer Roadmap

Open and free, no paywall. 9 phases, 60+ modules, 3 capstones, with embedded YouTube lessons and
account-synced progress tracking at https://balajichippada.com/roadmap

## Phase 1 — Python Foundations (Weeks 1–3, 6 modules)

- 1.1 Core Python — variables, functions, comprehensions, type hints
- 1.2 Object-Oriented Python — classes, dataclasses, Pydantic
- 1.3 Working with HTTP APIs — requests, auth, retries
- 1.4 Database Connectivity — PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, pooling
- 1.5 FastAPI — endpoints, dependency injection, OpenAPI
- 1.6 Async Programming — asyncio, gather, timeouts

## Phase 2 — LLM Mental Model (Week 4, 5 modules)

- 2.1 What an LLM actually is
- 2.2 How an LLM thinks — tokenization, context, sampling
- 2.3 Reasoning models vs base models
- 2.4 Reading model evals & benchmarks
- 2.5 Comparing major models (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, etc.)

## Phase 3 — Prompt Engineering & API Access (Weeks 5–7, 7 modules)

- 3.1 UI vs API
- 3.2 Calling LLMs via API (OpenAI, Anthropic SDKs)
- 3.3 Prompt anatomy
- 3.4 Core techniques (zero-shot, few-shot, COSTAR)
- 3.5 Applied patterns (extraction, classification, generation)
- 3.6 Advanced reasoning (CoT, self-consistency, self-refine)
- 3.7 Prompt management, caching, DSPy

## Phase 4 — RAG + Evaluation (Weeks 8–12, 9 modules)

- 4.1 Why RAG exists
- 4.2 Embeddings
- 4.3 Document ingestion (Docling)
- 4.4 Chunking strategies
- 4.5 Chunk enrichment (PII, NER)
- 4.6 Vector databases (Pinecone, pgvector, Chroma)
- 4.7 Hybrid retrieval & reranking
- 4.8 Graph-augmented RAG (Neo4j)
- 4.9 RAG evaluation (RAG Triad, Ragas, golden datasets)

**Capstone 1**: Distributed Document Ingestion + RAG Pipeline

## Phase 5 — Tools, MCP, Single Agents (Weeks 13–16, 8 modules)

- 5.1 Function calling / tool use
- 5.2 Tool design principles
- 5.3 MCP (Model Context Protocol)
- 5.4 ReAct pattern
- 5.5 LangChain agents
- 5.6 Human in the loop
- 5.7 Tool security
- 5.8 Computer use & app SDKs

## Phase 6 — Memory & Context Engineering (Weeks 17–19, 7 modules)

- 6.1 Context window as working memory
- 6.2 SYSTEM / CONTEXT / USER separation
- 6.3 Short-term session history
- 6.4 Semantic caching (FAISS)
- 6.5 Episodic memory
- 6.6 Context compression
- 6.7 Long-term memory (mem0, Zep)

## Phase 7 — Multi-Agent Orchestration (Weeks 20–22, 8 modules)

- 7.1 When to go multi-agent
- 7.2 LangGraph fundamentals
- 7.3 Common patterns (supervisor, pipeline, reflection)
- 7.4 Agent-as-tool
- 7.5 State management & checkpointers
- 7.6 A2A protocol
- 7.7 Framework comparison
- 7.8 Debugging multi-agent systems

**Capstone 2**: Multi-agent orchestration system

## Phase 8 — Guardrails & LLMOps (Weeks 23–24, 4 modules)

- 8.1 Three-layer guardrail architecture
- 8.2 AWS Bedrock Guardrails
- 8.3 Observability (LangSmith, LangFuse)
- 8.4 Production evaluation & drift detection

## Phase 9 — Cloud Infrastructure & Deployment (Weeks 25–26, 6 modules)

- 9.1 Storage (S3, RDS, DynamoDB)
- 9.2 Compute (Lambda, ECS Fargate)
- 9.3 Networking (VPC, IAM, API Gateway)
- 9.4 AI services (Bedrock, Vertex, Azure AI)
- 9.5 Deployment & streaming (SSE, WebSockets)
- 9.6 Cost & capacity control

**Capstone 3**: Production agent on AWS

## Course vs. free roadmap

The YouTube channel and the roadmap explain the concepts and will always stay free. They are
one-way: nothing checks whether you built anything. The course adds one enforced sequence, quizzes,
reviewed assignments, capstones, the Atlas product you keep upgrading, 24-hour doubt support,
weekly live sessions, mock interviews, resume prep, and biweekly updates.

- Roadmap overview: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eze6D8jAMjI
- YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/@balajichippada (35K+ subscribers, 230K+ roadmap views)
- Per-module deep-dive videos embedded on the interactive site

## Instructor

Balaji Chippada — production agentic AI engineer and educator, 9+ years in AI/ML. Production
experience at Swisscom, Warner Bros. Discovery, T-Mobile and Infosys. 5,000+ students and working
professionals mentored over the last three years.

## FAQ (common questions)

Q: Is the course for beginners?
A: Yes, completely. Python is taught inside the course; no prior coding or AI background is needed.

Q: Is the roadmap free?
A: Yes — open, no paywall, and staying that way. Masterclasses are separate live sessions (some
free, some paid). The course is the paid, structured track.

Q: How is the course different from YouTube?
A: YouTube tells you what to learn. The course makes sure you build it — enforced sequence,
quizzes, reviewed assignments, capstones, 24-hour doubt support, live sessions, mock interviews.

Q: Does the course get you a job?
A: No guarantees are made. It covers what the market hires for (RAG, agents, MCP, evaluation,
deployment) and includes mock interviews and resume prep.

Q: Will it stay current?
A: Content is updated biweekly; 2 years of access covers every update in that window.
